$comment: Shared behaviour fixture for the score shorthand parser, read by BOTH
The two parseScoreShorthand implementations are byte-identical copies, and
nothing stops them drifting. Pointing both test suites at this one file is
what makes a divergence fail rather than go unnoticed. A TO cannot recover
a score that was reported wrong, so this is the code where equivalence has
to be provable rather than assumed.
'games' is one character per game from the SET WINNER's perspective: W = the
set winner won that game, L = they lost it. 'errorContains' pins which
rejection fires, not its exact prose.
'fn' says which function a case applies to, so a suite can run only the

cases.name: sweep: + is a clean bo3 win
sweep: + is a clean bo5 win — the same input sized by requiredWins
sweep: 0 is the same sweep as +
sweep: a bare - is a sweep, NOT loss-mode with no digits
win-list: 124 is a bo5 3-1, and says so without needing requiredWins
win-list: 12 is a bo3 2-0
win-list: 13 is a bo3 2-1
loss form: -3 is a bo5 3-1 — the same set as 124 and WWLW
loss form: -1 is a bo3 2-1 with the loss first
loss form: -2 places the loss mid-set
loss form: -12 is a bo5 3-2
sequence: WWLW is a bo5 3-1 — the same set as 124 and -3
sequence: lowercase is accepted, since it is typed at speed
sequence: WLW is a bo3 2-1
surrounding whitespace is ignored
rejects empty input
rejects whitespace-only input the same way
rejects non-ascending game numbers — 121 cannot be a set
rejects a repeated game number
rejects 0 as a game number — games are 1-indexed
rejects a loss form with a 0 in it
rejects a double minus
rejects letters that are not w or l
rejects a sequence that does not end in a win for the set winner
cases.errorContains: last game of the set has to be a win

cases.name: rejects a loss form whose final game would be the loss
cases.errorContains: last game of the set has to be a win

cases.name: rejects a loss on the game after the winner already clinched
cases.errorContains: last game of the set has to be a win

cases.name: rejects the winner taking more games than the set can contain
rejects a bo3 win-list that only fits a bo5
rejects a sequence continuing past the winner's clinch
rejects the loser reaching requiredWins — they would have won the set
rejects a sequence giving the loser requiredWins

cases.$comment: A set is over when someone reaches requiredWins, so the winner must have exactly that many. Bounding only the upper side let a score describing an unfinished set through, and it would have been reported as final.
cases.name: rejects a bo3 1-0 — the set is not over
rejects a bo3 1-1 — nobody has won yet
rejects a bo5 2-0 — two wins do not finish a best of five
rejects a win list that stops short of the win requirement
rejects a bo5 sequence that only reaches two wins
the same two-win score is still valid at bo3, where it does finish the set
a loss form still reaches the requirement, so it stays valid
